signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: The AUD/CHF cross has emerged as the dominant G10 trend, with the AUD 1W average outperforming at +1.297% while the CHF laggard falls -0.783%. This 2.080% leader-to-laggard spread is supported by a significant +435bp carry advantage for AUD (RBA 4.35% vs SNB 0.0%). Speculative positioning in AUD is crowded long with a 52-week percentile of 94 (z=+1.78), while CHF remains net short at the 19th percentile. Low volatility (VIX 14.5) sustains the carry-seeking environment, though the extreme AUD long positioning suggests the theme is mature. Technical support for AUD/USD sits at the SMA20/50 cluster near 0.7013-0.7094. Trade bias: Long AUD/CHF; carry advantage remains the primary driver in a low-volatility regime. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — hold expected. Risk: VIX spikes above 20, triggering a rapid unwind of the AUD/CHF carry trade.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Intervention Risk + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 160.16, holding above the 160.00 psychological level which historically triggers BoJ verbal warnings and intervention risk. Despite a +275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage supporting the pair, the options market is pricing in heavy downside protection with a 25d Risk Reversal of -1.81. This strong put skew indicates that institutional desks are hedging for a sharp reversal despite the spot trend. BoJ's Himino recently highlighted inflation risks, reinforcing the OIS hike bias, while USD positioning remains net long (lev_net +8,110). A break back below the SMA50 at 160.86 would suggest the intervention threat is capping upside. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; 160.00 level introduces asymmetric intervention risk against a crowded carry trade. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 69% hike priced) 18 Sep. Risk: Fed Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole delivers a hawkish surprise, driving USD/JPY higher regardless of BoJ threats.

signals.title: AUD/USD — COT Extreme + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD shows a significant divergence between institutional and retail participants at the 0.7160 level. Leveraged funds are heavily net long AUD at +49,749 contracts, marking the 94th percentile of the 52-week range (z=+1.78), while retail sentiment is 90% short. This extreme retail fade against institutional momentum often precedes a final trend extension or a sharp 'stop-run' before exhaustion. The RBA's restrictive real rate of +0.85% supports the AUD bid against the USD's -9.6 ESI score. However, the WoW delta of +4,022 suggests adds are still active, reducing the immediate risk of a long-unwind. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD, supported by institutional-retail divergence and carry. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep. Risk: A sudden shift in global risk appetite (VIX > 20) forces leveraged funds to liquidate crowded AUD longs.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Macro Hedge
signals.text: GBP/USD is trading at 1.3529, underpinned by a SONIA-SOFR OIS differential that slightly favors the Pound (-9bp carry). The pair exhibits an elevated Vol Risk Premium (VRP) of +5.9%, with 1M IV at 11.0% vs a realized HV30 of 5.1%. This suggests the options market is paying a high premium for protection ahead of BoE Governor Bailey's comments on muted inflation. While COT positioning is crowded long at the 92nd percentile (z=+1.22), the negative ESI score of -9.3 for the UK provides a fundamental headwind. The technical position remains constructive as the pair holds above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3418-1.3537). Trade bias: Neutral/range GBP/USD; high vol premium reflects caution despite bullish technicals. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep. Risk: US NFP benchmark revisions (down 79k) lead to a broader USD sell-off, pushing Cable through 1.3600.
